name: Pressure Washing
tagline: Driveways, paving, house wash, decks, fences, commercial areas

emergency: water running into the switchboard or power points
chemical splash in the eyes or on skin
gas smell near the work area
urgent: cracked render or brick damaged by washing
fibro cladding that may need testing
oil or chemical spill on the driveway
graffiti on a shopfront before opening

extra_prompt: You are booking for a pressure washing company. Ask the surface type (concrete, brick, timber, render, roof tiles, or vinyl), because some surfaces need soft washing or low pressure. Ask the approximate area in square metres or the number of rooms or levels. Ask whether water and power are available on site. For roofs and high work, offer a site assessment and do not quote from a photo alone. Ask about loose paint, timber rot, or cracks, which may need repair before cleaning.

kb.q: Will pressure washing damage my house?
kb.a: Not when it is done correctly. We choose the pressure, nozzle and cleaning product for each surface, and we use low-pressure soft washing on painted, timber and delicate surfaces.

kb.q: Can you clean a fibro or fibre cement wall?
kb.a: Fibro can contain asbestos. We do not pressure wash fibro. We arrange an assessment, and any cleaning is done with low-pressure methods only after the surface is confirmed safe.

kb.q: How much does it cost to pressure wash a driveway?
kb.a: {price_note} Driveways are usually priced by the square metre, with a minimum charge. The price depends on size, surface type, and how much staining there is.

kb.q: Do you clean pavers and concrete?
kb.a: Yes. We clean pavers, concrete and exposed aggregate, and we remove moss, oil stains and dirt. We can also reset the joint sand if needed.

kb.q: Can you remove oil stains from my driveway?
kb.a: Often yes. Fresh oil responds well to a degreaser, while old stains may need several treatments. We tell you the likely result before we start.

kb.q: Do you wash the house or only the walls?
kb.a: We wash walls, eaves, and the lower parts of the house using soft wash. Roofs are cleaned only with methods that do not damage tiles or sheets.

kb.q: What is soft washing?
kb.a: Soft washing uses low pressure with a biodegradable cleaning solution to remove mould, algae and grime. It is safer for painted and delicate surfaces.

kb.q: Do you clean decks?
kb.a: Yes. We clean and brighten timber and composite decks. We can also prepare decks for staining or sealing, and we advise on timber that may be too soft for pressure.

kb.q: Can you clean my fence?
kb.a: Yes. We clean timber, colorbond and vinyl fences. Timber that is old or weathered may need low pressure to avoid raising the grain.

kb.q: Can you remove graffiti?
kb.a: Yes. We remove graffiti from brick, concrete and metal where the surface can take it. Some surfaces may be marked or dulled, and we tell you before we start.

kb.q: Do you seal the driveway after cleaning?
kb.a: Yes. We can apply a penetrating or film-forming sealer. Sealing should wait until the surface is dry, which can take a few days after washing.

kb.q: How long does pressure washing last?
kb.a: Driveways and paving typically look clean for several months to a year, depending on traffic, shade and the area. Sealing can extend this.

kb.q: Do you do commercial pressure washing?
kb.a: Yes. We wash shopfronts, loading docks, bin areas, car parks and building exteriors, often outside business hours.

kb.q: Can you clean before a property sale?
kb.a: Yes. A pre-sale exterior clean is quick and makes a big difference to kerb appeal. We can book a visit before inspection days.

kb.q: Do you need water and power on site?
kb.a: We need access to a water tap and, for larger jobs, a power point. Tell us if the supply is limited so we can plan the job.

kb.q: Will the chemicals harm my plants?
kb.a: We protect garden beds and plants with covers and rinse them after treatment. Tell us which plants are sensitive, and we will take extra care.

kb.q: Is pressure washing safe around pets and children?
kb.a: We ask people and pets to stay clear of the work area during and for a short time after the wash. We rinse surfaces before they are used again.

kb.q: Can you clean rooftops?
kb.a: We clean some roofs with soft wash methods that suit the roof type. We do not use high pressure on tiles or sheets, and we do not walk on fragile roofs.

kb.q: Do you clean gutters?
kb.a: We can clean the outside of gutters and rinse the downpipes. For full gutter clearing, a roofing or gutter service may be better.

kb.q: Are you insured?
kb.a: Yes. We carry public liability insurance for our work on site, and we can send a certificate of currency on request.

kb.q: What if the stains do not come out?
kb.a: We tell you before we start what is realistic. If a stain does not respond, we stop, explain why, and suggest the next step.

kb.q: How do I prepare for a pressure wash?
kb.a: Move vehicles and pot plants, close windows and doors, and remove loose items from the area. We handle the rest and tell you if anything needs covering.

kb.q: Do you clean outdoor furniture?
kb.a: Yes. We clean outdoor furniture, including timber, metal and some plastic items, using a gentle method on delicate pieces.

kb.q: Do you pressure wash swimming pool surrounds?
kb.a: Yes. We clean pool surrounds and pavers. We do not clean inside the pool itself, which is done by a pool service.
